statements.quote: The Born reciprocity principle states that the validity of quantum mechanics implies a fundamental symmetry between space and momentum space. This symmetry results from the freedom to choose a basis of states. General relativity fundamentally breaks this symmetry because it states that spacetime is curved, while energy-momentum space, defined as a cotangent space, is linear and flat.
statements.reading: FLM place the breaking of Born reciprocity in general relativity's flat momentum space, not in a vacuum. #11 §3 makes the same diagnosis ('general relativity's flat momentum fibers — the last an architectural assumption'); FLM had it in 2013.

statements.quote: Thus, we see that it is a matter of convention that we have taken \bar{p} to vanish.
statements.reading: For the flat string, which of X and its Fourier dual Y carries the quasi-period, and so which is read as spacetime, is a convention. The two are related by a Fourier transform, which is T-duality in the compact case. The choice is called conventional, not physical.

statements.quote: And finally, we relax the condition on \eta to be a flat metric, i.e. we allow it to be arbitrary curved. These generalizations restore the Born duality symmetry.
statements.where: 'First order formalism and the phase space action' paragraphs
statements.reading: A curved, dynamical η is said to restore Born duality. The breaking is blamed on the fixed flat structures of the usual formulation, not on a vacuum.

statements.quote: One can show [15] that solutions of the classical string EOM associated with a chiral structure (\eta,J) on \cal P are in correspondence with transversal bi-Lagrangian distributions.
statements.reading: The choice of bi-Lagrangian, which fixes which Lagrangian is spacetime, labels solutions of the equations of motion. My reading: this makes the choice a property of a solution, which is where a vacuum would carry it, but FLM neither call it a vacuum choice nor analyse it as symmetry breaking.

statements.quote: In this formulation both elements (\eta,J) of the chiral structure are dynamical. The solutions are labelled by bi-Lagrangians and spacetime is a derived dynamical concept.
statements.reading: This is the earliest school statement found that the choice of spacetime inside phase space is dynamical (2013). The record already quotes it (notes/toy-lagrangian.md; the wiki page on broken Born duality). It gives no potential, no order parameter and no vacuum analysis.

statements.quote: We have presented a new viewpoint on string theory, with wide ramifications and applications ranging from the stringy uncertainty principle [6, 9, 8] to “non-compact” T-duality [25], including the vacuum problem in string theory.
statements.reading: 'The vacuum problem' here means the string-vacuum problem, listed as an application. Nothing in the letter ties it to the choice of polarization.

statements.quote: Note that the 2d electrostatic picture of the correlation functions of the usual vertex operators [6] (see also [8]) now generalizes to 2d electromagnetism with electric and magnetic charges (dyons), if we allow vertices with both p,\bar{p} . The corresponding Dirac-Schwinger-Zwanziger quantization of the dyon charges is equivalent to satisfying the diffeomorphism constraint in the presence of these operators [15].
statements.where: 'Quasi-Periodicity and generalized T-duality', paragraph on relaxed boundary conditions
statements.reading: These are worldsheet (2d) charges. Momentum p acts as electric charge and winding p̄ as magnetic charge of dyonic vertex operators, and their Dirac–Schwinger–Zwanziger quantization is the diffeomorphism (level-matching) constraint. They are not magnetically charged objects in spacetime or in momentum space. My comparison: this is a school precedent for #11 §11.3's symplectic charge lattice, not for §11.4.

papers.summary: In this 2013 letter, Born reciprocity is a basis-choice symmetry that GR's flat momentum space breaks. Making η curved restores it. Solutions of the string equations are labelled by bi-Lagrangians, so 'spacetime is a derived dynamical concept'. In flat space, which of X and Y is spacetime is 'a matter of convention'. There is no vacuum mechanism, potential, order parameter or spontaneous breaking, and no dark matter.

statements.quote: One of the central insights of Born, 75 years ago [3], was to notice that the kinematical symmetry generated by I is fundamentally broken in the presence of gravity.
statements.reading: This is where the word 'kinematical' comes from. The Born symmetry is kinematical, and gravity breaks it. FLM credit the observation to Born.

statements.quote: It is important to appreciate that this kinematical breaking is different from the dynamical breaking that arises in Schrödinger’s quantum mechanics, due to the choice of a particular Hamiltonian. In the latter case we can still change the basis of states.
statements.reading: FLM separate two cases. 'Kinematical breaking' is GR's, where no change of basis is possible. 'Dynamical breaking' is the explicit breaking by a chosen Hamiltonian in quantum mechanics. Neither is spontaneous breaking in the program's sense, a symmetric law with an asymmetric vacuum.

statements.quote: There is a preferred basis — the space-time basis. According to Born, the clash between the kinematical duality symmetry of quantum mechanics and the presence of dynamical space-time curvature is what prevents us from a theory of quantum gravity. In other words, a theory of quantum gravity ought to restore the kinematical duality principle.
statements.reading: FLM aim to restore the duality, not to break it. Their preferred spacetime basis is a defect of GR that quantum gravity should remove. Compare #11 §3, where the breaking is mandatory and spontaneous.

statements.quote: In pure quantum mechanics, H is a kinematical structure, while \eta or the choice of preferred polarization, can be modified by unitary dynamics. Alternatively, in pure gravity \eta is a kinematical structure (space-time provides a preferred polarization that cannot be modified), while H , or at least its space-time part, becomes dynamical.
statements.where: §1.3 Summary: Quantum gravity and dynamical phase space
statements.reading: η is identified with 'the choice of preferred polarization'. In GR it is kinematical; in quantum mechanics it can be changed by unitary evolution.

statements.quote: Moreover if we introduce quantum theory in gravity, we have to make \eta dynamical. This is our addition to Born’s argument [1].
statements.reading: FLM claim a dynamical η, the structure that encodes the polarization, as their own addition (2013–2014). #11 P2′ credits this: 'That η should be dynamical rather than fixed was argued independently in metastring theory'.

statements.quote: It is important to note that the kinematical nature of \eta in gravity is tied up with the assumption of locality, i.e., the existence of a single well-defined space-time for all matter probes. Therefore a dynamical \eta necessarily leads to a relaxation of locality and a breakdown of effective field theory.
statements.reading: For FLM a dynamical η relaxes locality. My comparison: in #11 §3 the selection of a polarization is what makes local physics possible ('any world with local physics must select a Lagrangian polarization'). The two treat the link between η and locality in opposite directions.

statements.quote: Moreover, the purely kinematical splitting of phase space into space and momentum space has to be made dynamical, and thus both the phase space metric H_{AB} and the neutral metric \eta_{AB} have to be dynamical in the context of quantum gravity.
statements.reading: The splitting, that is the polarization, is to be made dynamical. This is FLM's proposal, against the kinematical splitting of GR.

statements.quote: This formulation does not require the presence of a bi-Lagrangian structure K . However when we look at solutions of string theory, we find this extra structure.
statements.where: §2 String Theory and Dynamical Phase Space
statements.reading: The action carries no K, the structure that tells space from momentum, but solutions do. My inference: a law without K whose solutions carry K is the logical form of a symmetry broken by the solution, the structure the program calls spontaneous breaking. FLM do not use that word, do not compare solutions by energy, and give no potential. This sentence is not in the record.

statements.quote: This null subspace is the effective space-time experienced by the string solution and is defined to be the Lagrangian sub-manifold with K=+1 . In this sense, different strings propagate in different space-time backgrounds which are made consistent via string interactions and through a dynamical momentum space [6], thus giving a sharp example of relative locality [5].
statements.reading: The spacetime is a property of each string solution and can differ from probe to probe (relative locality). Agreement comes from interactions. This differs from P5, where one vacuum selects for all matter.

statements.quote: When this Lagrangian manifold is assumed to be a fixed kinematical \eta -null subspace (which requires \eta to be kinematical) then we recover the usual Polyakov formulation where all strings propagate in the same fixed Lagrangian subspace, called space-time. But we see that this special case happens only when \eta is kinematical, and not dynamical.
statements.reading: The usual, universal spacetime is the special case of a kinematical η. FLM's general case has a dynamical η.

statements.quote: In order to generalize one of the key properties of T-duality, it is natural to demand that J maps the space-time Lagrangian K=1 onto the momentum space Lagrangian K=-1 .
statements.reading: T-duality (J) exchanges the spacetime and momentum-space Lagrangians, so the other choice is related to this one by a symmetry. Compare P5's 'the mirror vacuum is equally lawful'.

statements.quote: the usual dynamical space-time picture appears only as an induced concept (the choice of a Lagrangian submanifold in a dynamical bi-Lagrangian structure) on equal footing with its complementary and likewise induced dynamical momentum space picture (the choice of a dual Lagrangian submanifold in the same dynamical bi-Lagrangian structure).
statements.reading: The spacetime and momentum-space pictures are 'on equal footing', and both are induced by a choice inside a dynamical structure.

statements.quote: The first two equations show that both metrics H and \eta are indeed dynamical. Since schematically \Box_{\eta}H=\partial_{X}\partial_{P}H , the last equation essentially says that the phase space metric can depend only on X or only on P . In the first case, we recover the usual graviton mode propagation on this space-time.
statements.where: §2.2 Two scale Renormalization Group, after eq. (2)
statements.reading: These are linearized background equations from a fixed point of a double RG. They restrict H to depend on X only or on P only: the field equations confine it to one section but do not say which. Only the X case is developed. The record has this (notes/toy-lagrangian.md: 'solved along either null line').

papers.summary: This is the key text for 'kinematical'. FLM call GR's breaking of the Born symmetry 'kinematical breaking' and credit it to Born. They argue that quantum gravity should restore the symmetry by making the splitting of phase space dynamical ('we have to make η dynamical. This is our addition to Born's argument'). In their string formulation the action needs no K and solutions carry it, and linearized background equations make H depend 'only on X or only on P'. There is no potential, order parameter, Goldstone mode or 'spontaneous', and no dark matter.

statements.quote: In ordinary quantum mechanics we may, depending on convenience, choose a position or momentum basis of states; it is a fundamental property of quantum theory that this choice of polarization is immaterial. In quantum gravity, if all probes agree on what we mean by space-time, then we have broken Born duality — there is a preferred choice of polarization, the space-time one.
statements.reading: This is the passage #11 §3 quotes, and it is on p. 3 as cited. The preferred polarization comes from agreement among probes (absolute locality), not from a vacuum.

statements.quote: In the absence of interactions amongst strings, it is perhaps not obvious that different strings should view the same Lagrangian submanifold as space-time.
statements.reading: Without interactions each probe could pick its own Lagrangian. Here the choice is per probe, not per vacuum.

statements.quote: Colloquially, it is only when probes talk to one another, through interactions, that they compare their choices.
statements.reading: Agreement on a spacetime is made by interactions between probes (relative locality). No mechanism or vacuum is given.

statements.quote: In the context of the metastring, the rigidity of the quantum theory is encoded into the flatness of the polarization metric \eta
statements.reading: FLM put the rigidity of quantum theory in a flat η, and they mean to relax it. P2′ puts rigidity in ω ('symplectic rigidity ≡ constancy of ℏ') and makes η emergent. Both make η non-rigid, but they disagree on what stays rigid.

statements.quote: However, the Born proposal is not enough. As we have pointed out in [3], in the metastring theory we must take \eta to be dynamical as well. As we have seen above, it is \eta that governs the splitting of phase space into space and momentum space.
statements.where: §2.1 More General Backgrounds and Born Geometries, p. 11
statements.reading: η governs the splitting, and in [26S] itself it must be dynamical.

statements.quote: It is relative locality that suggests that both \eta and H be dynamical. In particular, in canonical quantum theory H is a purely kinematical structure and \eta , which describes the choice of polarization, can be modified by unitary dynamics. Conversely, in the context of gravitational dynamics, \eta is a purely kinematical structure (because space-time provides the preferred basis or polarization), while H , through its space-time part, can be made dynamical.
statements.reading: η 'describes the choice of polarization'. It is kinematical only in GR.

statements.quote: When we introduce quantum theory into gravity, we have to make the neutral metric \eta dynamical, and thus in the context of quantum gravity, both H and \eta have to be dynamical.
statements.reading: The paper #11 cites for the 'kinematical' attribution makes the polarization metric dynamical in quantum gravity. #11 P2′ credits this, which #11 §3's 'They treat the breaking as kinematical' does not reflect.

statements.quote: not only the constant Q-metric H^{0} is promoted to an arbitrarily curved metric H , but also the P-metric and symplectic structure are allowed to be dynamical.
statements.where: §2.3 Usual string viewed from phase space
statements.reading: In the metastring ω is dynamical as well as η and H (eq. 41 calls all three 'dynamical'). P2′ keeps ω rigid, so the school's dynamical η comes in a setting that P2′ excludes.

statements.quote: This generalization is one of the most interesting and will need to be dynamically constrained in order to give admissible backgrounds. In particular, it implies considering the new possibility where \eta is no longer a flat metric. This entails relaxing the condition that the splitting between space-time and energy-momentum is universal.
statements.reading: A curved η means the splitting is no longer universal. The constraints are to come from dynamics and are not given.

statements.quote: By keeping the property of maximal degeneracy, we keep the concept of a preferred Lagrangian defined by the metastring fields.
statements.reading: The preferred Lagrangian is ker(η+ω), a property of the background fields of the sigma model. It is defined, not selected.

statements.quote: In that respect it is interesting to note that the condition of absolute locality follows from the demand of worldsheet locality of observables.
statements.reading: A consistency condition, worldsheet locality, leads to a single spacetime for all fields, the L-projectability condition. This is a kinematical selection, as #11 §3 says, though it confines fields to one section without saying which.

statements.quote: What is new about this viewpoint is that it allows us to think about the choice of space-time inside phase space as a dynamical question.
statements.where: §7 Quantum Lagrangians and Modular Space-time, p. 47 (v1 PDF)
statements.reading: This is the phrase #11 §3 quotes. It is on p. 47, not p. 3, and #11 gives no page for it. The words are 'the choice of space-time inside phase space', not 'the breaking'.

statements.quote: What is conceptually remarkable here is that this target space locality condition is selected by demanding worldsheet locality.
statements.reading: The selector actually exhibited in this paper is a consistency requirement (worldsheet locality), not an energetic or vacuum mechanism.

statements.quote: Allowing the notion of space-time to be dynamical goes hand in hand with allowing the \eta metric to become dynamical. In the metastring formulation new CFT deformation modes are allowed, including the winding modes, whose collective excitations correspond to deformations of the \eta background.
statements.reading: η has field excitations: winding-mode collective excitations deform it. This is the nearest thing in the paper to η as a field with its own modes. No potential or vacuum analysis is given.

statements.quote: Also, in this formulation T-duality exchanges the Lagrangian sub-manifold with its orthogonal complement.
statements.reading: The other choice is the T-dual one, related by a symmetry of string theory and so equally lawful.

statements.quote: it may offer new insights into standard problems in string theory, such as vacuum selection.
statements.reading: This is the only use of 'vacuum selection': a hope about the string-vacuum problem, not about the polarization. The paper has no 'spontaneous', 'order parameter' or 'Goldstone' (0 hits).

papers.summary: This is #11's [26S]. The §3 quotation is on p. 3 and 'a dynamical question' is on p. 47 (§7). The paper makes η, which 'describes the choice of polarization', dynamical (§2.1), and ω and H as well (§2.3). The selector it exhibits is worldsheet locality (§6.1, §7), and T-duality exchanges L with its complement (§8). 'Vacuum selection' appears once, as a hope about string vacua. There is no 'spontaneous', order parameter, potential on η or Goldstone mode, and no dark matter.

statements.quote: The paradox is resolved by recognizing that an observer’s notion of space corresponds to a choice of basis (a choice of polarization), and such a notion is acted upon by rotations. However, precisely because the underlying algebra is non-commutative, any such choice is unitarily equivalent to any other, and thus the action of rotations induces a superposition of modular spaces.
statements.reading: A polarization is the observer's choice of basis, and every choice is unitarily equivalent to every other. In this paper the polarization is not a physical vacuum choice.

statements.quote: The basic definition that we propose for a quantum space is that it is a choice of polarization for the representation of the Heisenberg algebra.
statements.reading: Space is defined as a choice of polarization. The paper does not say what makes the choice.

statements.quote: As a summary, we have seen that the choice of modular quantization \alpha_{\eta} is associated with the choice of a polarization metric \eta which determines a bilagrangian lattice (\Lambda,\eta) , also called Narain lattices.
statements.reading: η enters as a parameter of the quantization, a choice, not as a field with a vacuum value.

statements.quote: This is indeed the most natural choice and it shows that we cannot fully disentangle the kinematics (i.e., the definition of translation generators) from the dynamics.
statements.reading: The modular vacuum is defined as the ground state of an 'energy' E_H = H^{AB}P_A P_B, so it depends on a chosen H. FLM say this mixes kinematics with dynamics.

statements.quote: Although we are using the term “Hamiltonian” here, the reader should not confuse it with the Hamiltonian of some particle system. Instead, it is a tool that we use to identify a “vacuum state of empty modular space.”
statements.reading: The 'Hamiltonian' that defines the vacuum is a device. Nothing dynamical selects it.

statements.quote: the different vacua measure effectively in which quantum reference frame the system finds itself
statements.reading: Vacua for different complex structures are related by squeezing, and FLM liken them to Unruh-type frame dependence. A vacuum here labels a quantum reference frame.

statements.quote: We also see that the zeroes of the extensified vacuum states \Theta_{(\Lambda,k)}^{(N)} are aligned along a Lagrangian manifold given by the condition x:=(z-\bar{z})/2i=k/N ( see Fig. 3). The choice of Lagrangian is controlled by the choice of complex structure that enters the definition of the “Hamiltonian”.
statements.reading: This is the closest any text read comes to a vacuum picking a Lagrangian. The zeroes of the large-N vacuum line up along a Lagrangian, and the complex structure in the 'Hamiltonian' controls which one. But that complex structure is chosen, not determined by dynamics, and no potential or energetic comparison is made. Not in the record.

statements.quote: Within such an application, the lattice (and consequently a length scale) associated with the maximally commutative sub-group is set contextually by some experimental apparatus (such as a slit spacing).
statements.reading: In laboratory quantum mechanics the polarization lattice is set by the apparatus. The choice is contextual.

statements.quote: Consequently, if we do make this identification, in most experiments we can safely ignore the presence of a fundamental scale, as fluctuations along momentum directions are negligible compared to fluctuations in position directions.
statements.reading: Position directions look classical because the gravitational tension ε/λ ~ c⁴/G is large. This is a scale hierarchy offered as the reason, not a vacuum selection.

statements.quote: A choice of quantum polarization is a choice of basis, unitarily equivalent to any other. To reconcile these ideas, we must retool our thinking in terms of the superpositions of quantum spaces. This should be thought of as an implementation of the idea of relative locality [37].
statements.reading: Every polarization is equally lawful, in fact unitarily equivalent. The discussion is framed by relative locality, not by a selected vacuum.

statements.quote: We also discuss how the usual classical notion of space comes out as a form of thermodynamical limit of modular space while the Schrodinger space is a singular limit.
statements.reading: Classical space arises as a limit (extensification). The paper has no 'spontaneous', 'order parameter' or 'Goldstone' (0 hits).

papers.summary: A polarization is an observer's choice of basis, unitarily equivalent to any other. The modular vacuum is the ground state of a chosen 'Hamiltonian' E_H and depends on H. In extensified vacua the zeroes lie along a Lagrangian 'controlled by the choice of complex structure' in that 'Hamiltonian'. That is a link from vacuum to Lagrangian, but the complex structure is chosen, with no dynamics, potential or order parameter behind it. No dark matter.

statements.quote: Born reciprocity is the simple observation that the change of basis from the position to the energy basis (P → Q and Q → −P) is a fundamental kinematical symmetry of quantum mechanics (QM). Thus Born reciprocity is broken by the choice of the principle of absolute locality, the statement that the same spacetime is shared by all probes independently of their energy state or history.

'They treat the breaking as kinematical' therefore describes what they say of GR, not what they propose, and understates them. In other words the dual Lorentz symmetry that acts on the free one metaparticle state is broken. The symmetry breaking happens at the level of the vacuum sector, and thus a choice of ground state fixes a value of \delta .' Also: 'Once a dual boost is performed the new commuting decoupling coordinate is no longer x , but x^{\mu}+\alpha^{\mu\nu}\tilde{x}_{\nu}+\cdots' and 'the infrared Lorentz violation appears only for an old Universe, as the symmetry is restored as one goes back in time.'
contradicts_record.why:
The school does analyse a symmetry breaking tied to the choice of polarization, published before the program. A symmetry that moves which phase-space coordinate is the commuting spacetime coordinate is broken 'at the level of the vacuum sector', the ground state fixes the frame, and the symmetry is restored in the past. 'No symmetry-breaking analysis' is therefore too strong.
What holds: there is no potential, the word 'spontaneous' is absent, nothing is called an order parameter (δ is what the ground state fixes, but they do not name it so), and no Goldstone modes appear. The essay also says the dual symmetry 'is fundamentally broken at the quantum level' by λ, so it does not separate explicit from vacuum breaking. The broken group is the non-compact dual Lorentz group of the doubled (x, x̃) space at λ², not ρ on (x, p) at ℏ.
The program's own addition narrows to the spontaneous formulation proper: the name, η as order parameter, the potential, the toy models' U(1) Goldstone angle and the K-sign lock. The record nowhere quotes these passages; the earlier check read 2104.00802 only for C1.

A school paper posted before the program proposes a mechanism that selects the spacetime frame, both in the vacuum (the ground state) and dynamically (the expansion), and joins it to dual degrees of freedom as a candidate dark sector. It is a hedged proposal: a simple cosmological model, 'dark matter/energy' undecided, class II metaparticles rather than a dual Standard Model, and the doubled (x, x̃) space.
'No such mechanism' therefore holds only for a spontaneous-breaking mechanism with an order parameter and a potential. 'A vacuum that selects a polarization' joined to a dual dark sector is published, in this hedged form.
The quotation 'corresponds to a choice' is accurate (2407.06207 §3.3), but the sentence ends 'with a contextuality parameter λ', and §3.5 ties the polarization to 'the contextual nature of quantum measurement'. That is what this school paper says does the choosing.
